paper_metadata.title: Microband induced plasticity and the temperature dependence of the mechanical properties of a carbon-doped FeNiMnAlCr high entropy alloy

evidence.quote: The uniaxial mechanical properties of the high entropy alloy (HEA) Fe40.4Ni11.3Mn34.8Al7.5Cr6 doped with 1.1 at. % C have been determined for both the as-cast and recrystallized states at temperatures from 77-973 K.

The lattice friction stress, which results from the increase of the Peierls barrier, was the major contributor to the large yield strength at 77 K.
The higher yield strength of the recrystallized HEA at lower temperatures is mainly due to the strengthening from the grain boundaries.

The recrystallized HEA, however, shows larger tensile elongation than that of the as-cast HEA at 973 K, see Fig. 4c. This is because of the grain boundary sliding that occurs in the fine-grained (5 µm) HEA at 973 K [39].
The formation of microbands accounts for the excellent combination of strain hardening and ductility in the as-cast HEA [7].
The lack of microbands at 973 K is because dislocation climb can take place due to the thermal activation, and grain subdivision is no longer occurs during deformation.

the lattice friction stress exhibits a substantial increase at 77 K, which strongly impedes the movement of dislocations. This led to the as-cast HEA becoming very brittle at 77 K and fracture occurred at yielding during the tensile test.
The formation of microbands accounts for the excellent combination of strain hardening and ductility in the as-cast HEA [7].

Due to the formation of carbides, the carbon content in the f.c.c. matrix decreased from 1.1 at. % in the as-cast HEA to 0.8 at. % in the recrystallized HEA, which caused a 67 MPa reduction in the lattice friction stress at 293 K [8].
The lack of microbands at 973 K is because dislocation climb can take place due to the thermal activation, and grain subdivision is no longer occurs during deformation.
The higher yield strength of the recrystallized HEA at lower temperatures is mainly due to the strengthening from the grain boundaries.

The recrystallized HEA, however, shows larger tensile elongation than that of the as-cast HEA at 973 K, see Fig. 4c. This is because of the grain boundary sliding that occurs in the fine-grained (5 µm) HEA at 973 K [39].
